routes.label: Read the diameters from the coordinates

question:
Semicircles \(POQ\) and \(ROS\) pass through the center of circle \(O.\) What is the ratio of the combined areas of the two semicircles to the area of circle \(O?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2010_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The coordinate labels give the semicircle diameters directly. We can then use a right triangle to find the large circle's squared radius.

[Figure 1](figures/2010_AMC_8_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

Points \(P(-1,1)\) and \(Q(1,1)\) have the same vertical coordinate, so
\[
PQ=1-(-1)=2.
\]
Likewise, \(RS=2\). Each semicircle therefore has radius \(1\), making their combined area
\[
2\left(\frac12\pi\cdot1^2\right)=\pi.
\]
The axes meet at \(O\), so \(O=(0,0)\). Going from \(O\) to \(P(-1,1)\) involves a horizontal distance of \(1\) and a vertical distance of \(1\). These form the legs of a right triangle with hypotenuse \(OP\). Thus
\[
OP^2=1^2+1^2=2.
\]
Since \(OP\) is a radius of circle \(O\), that circle has area \(2\pi\). The requested ratio is
\[
\frac{\pi}{2\pi}=\boxed{\frac12},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
